papers.version_note: arXiv:1810.07552v2, compiled 6 December 2018; the text layer ends with a full-reference list.
papers.what_it_is: An Optics Letters paper that demonstrates selective sum-frequency upconversion of overlapping Laguerre-Gaussian spatial modes in a PPLN crystal by shaping the pump mode with a particle swarm optimizer and adaptive feedback.

assertions.value: The authors state that they pump a second-order nonlinear crystal with a laser in a tailored transverse mode, which gives selective conversion of signals in overlapping but orthogonal spatial modes with largely differential efficiencies.
quotes: here we pump a second-order nonlinear crystal with a laser in a tailored transverse mode
selective conversion of signals in overlapping but orthogonal spatial modes with largely differential efﬁciencies

assertions.value: The authors report in the abstract that, for signals in Laguerre-Gaussian modes, a mode can be converted with up to 60 times higher efficiency than an overlapping but orthogonal mode.
quotes: we show that a mode can be converted with up to 60 times higher efﬁciency than an overlapping but orthogonal mode
assertions.reader_inference: The 60 times figure is not stated again in the body. The body reports extinction up to 18 dB (about 63 times as a power ratio), which agrees roughly with 60 times.

assertions.value: The authors state that the spatial mode-selective conversion is implemented by sum-frequency generation in a periodically poled lithium niobate crystal, and that the pump and signal modes are each prepared with spatial light modulators.
quotes: Our spatial MSC is implemented through sum-frequency (SF) generation in a periodic-poled lithium niobate (PPLN) crystal
The pump and signal modes are each prepared by using spatial light modulators (SLMs)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the Introduction.

assertions.value: The authors state that they demonstrate mode-selective conversion of the Laguerre-Gaussian modes, and that the technique is applicable to other mode bases, including Hermite-Gauss modes. Only Laguerre-Gaussian modes are tested.
quotes: we demonstrate the MSC of the LG modes
The technique itself, however, is applicable to other mode basis
assertions.reader_inference: The applicability to Hermite-Gauss modes is stated without a test in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that they focus on sum-frequency generation in the non-diffraction regime, where the diffraction of the interacting waves through the crystal is not significant, and that diffraction would be exploited in future studies to achieve better performance.
quotes: diffraction regime, where the diffraction of the interacting waves
to achieve better performance
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the regime of its own model and experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pump field is a constant in the nondepletion pump approximation, which is the case in this study, and that under the quasi-phase matching condition the generated sum-frequency field follows their sum-frequency equation. They state that the equation is valid in the current parameter regime without strong diffraction.
quotes: is a constant in the nondepletion pump approximation, which is the case in this study
which is valid in the current parameter
regime without strong diffraction
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the model assumptions in the text around Equations 2 to 4.

assertions.value: The authors report that they measured the quasi-phase matching curve of the PPLN crystal by scanning a continuous-wave laser and measuring the generated second harmonic power, and fitted a sinc squared function. The caption reports a full width at half maximum phase matching bandwidth of about 6.5 nm centered at 1552 nm.
quotes: The FWHM phase matching bandwidth is about 6.5 nm centered at 1552 nm
by scanning a continuous-wave laser and measuring the generated second harmonic (SH) power

assertions.value: The authors report two continuous-wave lasers at 1558 nm and 1545 nm with a linewidth of at most 100 kHz, modulated into two pulse trains, each with 200 ps full width at half maximum and a 10 MHz repetition rate, and synchronized with a common radio-frequency reference source. They state that the wavelength difference is about 13 nm, so the group velocities are approximately equal in the crystal.

assertions.value: The authors report that the pump average power is 40 mW and peak power is 21 W, and that the signal average power is 35 mW and peak power is 18 W, after amplification with two erbium-doped fiber amplifiers.

average power is 35 mW and peak power is 18 W

The sum-frequency light is at 775.75 nm, and the Gaussian signal and pump beam waists inside the crystal are 45 µm and 41 µm.

quotes: The angle of incidence for the pump and signal beams onto the SLMs are about 50◦ and 55◦, respectively.

assertions.value: The authors define the relative conversion efficiency as the efficiency relative to that of a Gaussian pump with a Gaussian signal of the same beam waist and same total pulse energy. They define the conversion extinction between two signal modes as the ratio of their conversion efficiencies by the same pump.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with pump modes not yet optimized, there is no appreciable extinction, and that only a modest selectivity of 5 dB is achieved between two signal modes with the same Gaussian pump mode.
assertions.anchor: Section on Figure 2, p.2 and p.3
quotes: there is no appreciable extinction as the pump modes have yet to be optimized
only a modest selectivity of 5 dB is achieved between two signal modes
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints the modes as LG10 and LG00 in the original sentence; the quote here stops before them.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use a particle swarm optimization algorithm to numerically optimize the pump spatial modes for targeted signal modes, and that a particle corresponds to a set of weighted phase masks for Laguerre-Gaussian modes whose superposition produces the pump profile after the Fourier lens.
quotes: we use a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to numerically optimize the pump spatial modes for targeted signal modes
a particle corresponds to a set of weighted phase masks for LG modes, whose superposition produces the pump proﬁle after the Fourier lens
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own method.

assertions.value: The authors report that they compared the analytic results under the undepleted pump approximation with exact numeric results that take pump depletion into account, and found good agreement.
quotes: We also compare the analytic results obtained under the undepleted pump approximation and exact numeric results taking into count the pump depletion and found good agreement.
assertions.reader_inference: No numbers for this comparison are given in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because of phase errors in the SLM and imperfect alignment of the Gaussian beam with respect to the phase mask, the attained selectivity is reduced, and that they use adaptive feedback control, with two SLMs and a power meter automated through a MATLAB interface, to adaptively manipulate the pump phase mask on SLM-2 to optimize the selectivity between two signal modes.
assertions.anchor: Section on experiment, p.3, and Figure 3 caption
quotes: due to the phase errors in the SLM and the imperfect alignment of the Gaussian beam with respect to the phase mask, the attained selectivity is
we utilize adaptive feedback control in the experiment [41]
we adaptively manipulate phase mask for the SLM-2 to optimize the selectivity between the two signal modes

assertions.value: The authors describe the feedback algorithm in eight steps in the figure caption: generate initial phase masks, measure the up-converted power of two or more target modes, compute the extinction ratio r, check whether r reaches a target, generate new superposition coefficients and update the pump phase mask when it does not, repeat until the target is met, collect the optimum selectivity, then update the target phase mask on SLM-1 and repeat.
quotes: Step 4: Check if the optimization criteria, r ≥ rtarget, is met.
Step 5: If r < rtarget, generate the new superposition coefﬁcients for the mode basis and update the phase mask for SLM-2.
Step 6: Repeat Steps 2-5 until r ≥ rtarget.
assertions.certainty_reason: The caption states the algorithm of the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that pump P0+0 is designed to convert the LG00 mode while suppressing other modes. The simulation achieves extinctions of 6.5 dB, 13.1 dB and 20.9 dB for the three suppressed modes, and the experiment gives 5.9 dB, 12.1 dB and 18.1 dB.
assertions.anchor: Table 1 and text, p.3 and p.4
quotes: Pump P0+0 is designed to convert the LG00 mode while simultaneously suppressing
The simulation achieves an extinction of 6.5 dB, 13.1 dB, and 20.9 dB for each, while the experimental results are 5.9 dB, 12.1 dB, and 18.1 dB.
assertions.reader_inference: The prose names the suppressed modes LG01, LG02 and LG30; Table 1 prints LG10, LG20 and LG30. The paper is internally inconsistent here.

assertions.value: The authors report that pump P0−0 is designed to suppress the LG00 mode while converting three other modes. The numerically maximized extinctions are 16.5 dB, 20.4 dB and 21.7 dB, and the experimental results are 11.8 dB, 14.8 dB and 15.6 dB.
assertions.anchor: Table 1 and text, p.3 and p.4
quotes: Pump P0−0 is designed to suppress LG00
The numerically maximized extinctions are 16.5 dB, 20.4 dB, and 21.7 dB for each, while the experimental results are 11.8 dB, 14.8 dB, and 15.6 dB, respectively.
assertions.reader_inference: The prose names the converted modes LG10, LG20 and LG03; Table 1 prints LG30 for the third. The paper is internally inconsistent here.

assertions.value: The authors report that pump P0+1 is optimized to convert one mode against three others. The simulation gives extinctions of 6.6 dB, 14.5 dB and 22.4 dB, and the experiment gives 5.6 dB, 11.5 dB and 15.2 dB.
assertions.anchor: Table 1 and text, p.3 and p.4
quotes: Pump P0+1 is optimized to convert LG10 against LG20, LG30, and LG40
The simulation gives 6.6 dB, 14.5 dB, and 22.4 dB extinction for each, while the experiment produces 5.6 dB, 11.5 dB, and 15.2 dB.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experimental measurements are in good agreement with the numerical simulations without using any fitting parameter, which they say validates their approach.
quotes: are in good agreement with the numerical simulations without using any ﬁtting parameter, which validates our approach
assertions.reader_inference: In Table 1 every experimental extinction is lower than its simulated value: the gap is 0.6 to 4.7 dB. Agreement is therefore in trend, not in value, and the 'good agreement' wording is the authors' own.

assertions.value: The authors state in the summary that their experimental results achieve conversion extinction up to 18 dB, in good agreement with the numerical simulation without any fitting parameters.
quotes: Our experimental results, which achieve conversion extinction up to 18 dB, are in good agreement with the numerical simulation without the use of any ﬁtting parameters.
assertions.reader_inference: The largest experimental value in Table 1 is 18.1 dB (pump P0+0).

assertions.value: The authors state that the next step is to extend the technique to the high conversion regime with strong diffraction, where they expect even better performance, as evident in the time-frequency domain. This is not tested in the paper.
quotes: In the future, we will extend this method to the high conversion regime, where higher selectivities are expected
The next step will be to extend this technique to the high conversion regime with strong diffraction, where even better performance is expected.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states what it has not done.

assertions.value: The authors state that the nonlinear optics based approach may find applications in improving the signal-to-noise ratio to recognize an image pattern, in spatial mode de-multiplexing of higher-order modes for classical and quantum communications, and in mode-selective LiDAR.
quotes: The nonlinear optics based approach may ﬁnd novel applications such as improving the signal-to-noise ratio to recognize an image pattern
spatial mode de-multiplexing of higher-order modes for classical and quantum communications
